title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 75 (Damages for fraud in deposits)

content.overview: If a company fails to repay a deposit or interest within the period in section 74 or a further period allowed by the Tribunal, and the deposit was accepted with intent to defraud depositors or for a fraudulent purpose, every officer responsible for accepting it is personally liable without limitation for all or any losses or damages incurred by depositors.
content.glance: If a company fails to repay a deposit or interest within the period in section 74 or a further period allowed by the Tribunal, and the deposit was accepted with intent to defraud depositors or for a fraudulent purpose, every officer responsible for accepting it is personally liable without limitation for all or any losses or damages incurred by depositors.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 75 (Damages for fraud). If a company fails to repay a deposit or any interest within the period specified in section 74 or within any further time allowed by the Tribunal under section 74(2), and it is proved that the deposit was accepted with intent to defraud depositors or for a fraudulent purpose, every officer of the company who was responsible for accepting the deposit is personally responsible, without any limitation of liability, for all or any losses or damages incurred by depositors. The section requires both non-repayment within the applicable period and proof of fraudulent intent/purpose; it does not make every deposit default automatically fraudulent. Criminal consequences may arise separately under section 76A or section 447 where their elements are met. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Non-repayment trigger
sections.body: The company must have failed to repay a deposit or interest within the period specified in section 74 or a further time allowed by the Tribunal under section 74(2).

sections.heading: Fraudulent intent or purpose
sections.body: It must be proved that the deposit was accepted with intent to defraud depositors or for a fraudulent purpose. Mere non-repayment alone does not establish this element under section 75.

sections.heading: Personal civil liability
sections.body: Every officer responsible for accepting the deposit is personally responsible, without limitation of liability, for all or any losses or damages incurred by depositors.

sections.heading: Separate statutory routes
sections.body: Section 75 concerns civil liability for depositor losses/damages. Any criminal or penalty route under section 76A or section 447 must be assessed separately under its own elements.

hypotheticals.question: A company defaults in repaying deposits, but there is no evidence that the deposits were accepted with fraudulent intent. Does section 75 automatically impose personal liability on every officer?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 75 requires proof that the deposits were accepted with intent to defraud depositors or for a fraudulent purpose, in addition to non-repayment within the section 74 period or Tribunal-allowed extension. It applies to officers responsible for accepting the deposit.

hypotheticals.question: A deposit was accepted for a fraudulent purpose and remains unpaid beyond the section 74 period. Who may be personally liable under section 75?
hypotheticals.analysis: Every officer responsible for accepting the deposit is personally responsible, without limitation of liability, for all or any losses or damages incurred by depositors.

distinctions.left: Section 75 imposes personal civil liability for depositor losses/damages when non-repayment and fraudulent intent/purpose are proved.
distinctions.right: Section 76A and section 447 address separate criminal/penalty routes where their elements are satisfied.

misconceptions.trap: Treating every failure to repay a deposit as proof of fraud.
misconceptions.correction: Section 75 requires proof of intent to defraud depositors or a fraudulent purpose.

misconceptions.trap: Applying section 75 to all officers regardless of their role in accepting the deposit.
misconceptions.correction: The section identifies officers responsible for accepting the deposit.

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 75 civil damages as identical to the section 76A offence/penalty.
misconceptions.correction: Civil liability for losses/damages and criminal/penalty provisions are separate legal routes.
